City Rates and Taxes Fraud

By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Carte Blanche has an exclusive internal report at the City of Johannesburg's valuations department that shows mass fraud and corruption - 22 properties were devalued by more than R500 million.

Unique Selling Point:
The report has been hidden and none of the recommendations were implemented... including further investigations into employees bank accounts looking for bribes, criminal charges were not laid, disciplinary did not happen. It was hushed all up, and some of the employees accused of negligence were actually promoted. We will undercover this report in its detail, confront the employees and go to the owners of the buildings that were devalued and ask them about it...



Further information:
This house has a tax that is calculated every 4 years. Based on three factors: property, location, property’s around that one. Properties are a great investment and depending on the taxes, many choose to place their money in there.
However, the City of Johannesburg has numerous issues when it comes to property taxes... this is our story.
Currently the city of Johannesburg is in the midst of a battle, between head of the property unit Sihle More and their own board- Valuation appeal board. Sihle has locked out the valuation board members from 2008. This on the back of a report that was finalized last year October, and a year later has not been complied with. It raises a number of alarming finds including fraud, bribery etc.
But lets go back to the beginning: Explain story in 2008 - the board was appointed in 2008 by the MEC (creature of statute, act of parliament) to deal with the valuation roll – definition – this is where all the houses in a given city limit are evaluated, updated etc according to their section...They hear and decide appeals against decisions of a municipal valuer concerning objections...10% up or down value...they are also responsible for supplementary valuation rolls of which there have been 11 supplementary rolls since 2008; more than 22448 objections, 2489 appeals, 9652 automatic reviews. + COJs own objections – 13 406 objections, 4680 reviews, 815 appeals.
In many instances the values were inflated, or objection forms were lost and they had to resort to checking and verifying information on the land information system / geo information system. (Some of ratepayers weren’t even notified to appear for their objections). Lack of information as to how valuers arrived to their valuations. (Ms. More, Piet Eloff, Valuers of E – responsible).
It then became apparent that many of decisions of the board had not been implemented by the CoJ – incorporated in LIS system – responsibility of Edward Stevenson (IT specialist capturing the decisions). Board has no access to billing system – invoices or accounts sent to ratepayers.
They did their own investigation and found that about 12-14% error margin in the recordial of decisions. However this is in the boardroom, and they have been locked out.
Examples: Fourways mall total value of 1 billion rand in 27 september 2010. Appeal = R941.46 million and allocated. Still no captured. CoJ is losing hundreds of thousands, if not millions on lost rates and taxes over this 6 year period. More is blaming the board for this. More became obstructive... another appeal board 2013 valuation roll. 12-14%
Went to court on a urgent basis and they won September 28. However, More now wants to appeal. Did not comply with court order. He is back in his office now.
http://www.moneyweb.co.za/news/south-africa/breaking-judge-slams-city-of-joburg-with-cost-order/

REPORT: Mbali Maclare Kwa Zimbali (Pty) Ltd.
Shows that the office is a mess and full of maladministration:
The report found the following – Mbali Maclare – aka Renolda Maclare, a woman a week younger than me, had defrauded the city of millions. She decreased the value of 22 properties by more than 500,000,000 costing the city 35 million for 4 years. (Not sure if that p.a.)
Then there were those who assisted Mbali and were found to have been negligent in their duty’s – 3 of them have been promoted. One of them was a Ms. Harrison who was also implicated. There was also bribery – were Michael Blah was found guilty of taking a R2000 bribe.
This all happened under manager Sihle More, who was responsible for locking out the 2008 board.
Why is this important – cos the missing millions from the 2008 non-implementation that hole may have to be covered by us, and the report that no one has acted on show losses running into the millions – and who will have to pay for this loss? Us the rate payers. Expect huge increases in order for the city to recover.

Press Release:


Johannesburg Property Rates
How were several multi-million rand Johannesburg properties inexplicably devalued in order to lower rates and taxes? Carte Blanche unravels an internal report alleging fraud totalling almost half a billion rand in the City of Johannesburg’s property valuation department.


Script:


V/O: A whopping 8.2 billion rand of the City of Johannesburg’s R45 billion budget for comes from property rates and taxes. This money provides rate payers with infrastructure and basic services.
DEVI: “EVERY 4 YEARS YOUR PROPERTY IS VALUED BY A MUNICIPAL VALUATOR, YOUR RATES AND TAXES ARE THEN CALCULATED BASED ON THIS VALUE.”
VO: If your home is worth R5 million you would pay over R122 thousand in rates and taxes over a 4 year period. However, if the value was lowered to R3 million you would pay only R71 thousand for the same period, making it a difference of R50 thousand.
DEVI: “EXACTLY A YEAR AGO THIS REPORT WAS RELEASED, IT HIGHLIGHTED ALLEGED FRAUD AND CORRUPTION AT THE CITY OF JOHANNESBURG’S PROPERTY VALUATION SERVICES UNIT. THE FINDINGS WERE SHOCKING: 22 PROPERTIES HAD BEEN DEVALUED BY ALMOST 500 MILLION RANDS, THIS REPORT WAS NEVER MADE PUBLIC.”
VO: By lowering the municipal value of a property, an owner could save significant amounts on monthly rates and taxes. And when it comes to more expensive properties, the savings could run into millions.
VO: These 4 buildings were devalued by a total of R268-million, resulting in a loss of R19 million in rates and taxes owed to the City.
Sharon: “The loss to the city in terms of revenue or rates and taxes is about 8 million per annum. The report says 35 million.”
V/O: Forensic accountant Sharon Sabbagh was part of the finance committee as a ward councillor for the City of Johannesburg from 2006 to 2011. Property valuations were part of her portfolio.
Devi: In South Africa we’re used to talking in billions, so when you start saying you’re talking 35 million, 8 million, people think, ugh, small change?
Sharon: But that’s on 22 properties! 22 properties of 109 sampled. We have 852 000 properties on the roll. That’s a potential 172 000 properties that could have been manipulated.
Pandora: “If you go to lunch at a restaurant, and the bill is R1000 and two people say I’ve left my wallet, the restaurant will still collect 1000 rand, whether it’s paid by 8 people or 10 people.
V/O: “Hercules” and “Pandora” and are two sources inside the city’s property valuations unit. Their identities have been changed.
Pandora: “The budget of a council is a complex thing, the value may be reduced, but now you must manipulate the tariff to get to the same budget.”
Hercules: “It makes me feel that fraud and corruption pays off and that all these endeavours paying thousands of rands for these reports is money in a big black hole.”
V/O: This means it’s the good rate payers who have to pay for the missing millions.
V/O: Mbali Maclare is alleged to have been the mastermind behind the devaluations inside the property valuation unit. We set up a home and called her to see if she’d be willing to lower its municipal value for a reduction in rates.
Mbali: “Let’s get the valuation certificate, with the market value, that would suit you. Before we print it, I can always call you and say this is the market value, at what value do you want it?”
Sasha: I believe it’s 2.8 to 3 million, so would it be possible to decrease it to 2 million. I can’t afford the rates and taxes.”
Mbali: “Aaah, Ya....It will cost you R2000 from my side.”
[04:59] With the devaluing, I don’t know what needs to happen there.
[05:04]If it’s too high we need to lodge an objection.
VO: An objection can be lodged if property owners are not happy with their valuations. An objection letter is created in the city’s system and this has a unique number. The report explains how Mbali Maclare -only a candidate valuer – allegedly falsified objection letters by changing the details of a real objection letter, and creating a false one in which she would then alter the value, often, by millions.
Sharon: if they had put in an objection, it would have gone to the appeals board and the appeals board would have reviewed it, and it would have gone back to the original value. So they manipulated the system.
VO: According to the report Mbali allegedly also forged signatures and used the city’s resources to operate her private valuation company – Kwa Zimbali.
Hercules: “She is not registered with the SA council for valuers as a professional valuer, so she is not a valuer.”
Devi: “Were people saying that she took bribes from people to undervalue their properties?”
Hercules: “A lot of allegations were made, but the report puts it in perspective.”
DEVI: “DURING OUR INVESTIGATION, WE FOLLOWED THE TRAIL OF THE COMPANIES LINKED TO THE 22 PROPERTIES WHICH WERE DEVALUED. ONE NAME COMES UP, REBOSIS, FOUR OF THEIR PROPERTIES ARE MENTIONED IN THIS REPORT, WERE DEVALUED BY OVER R268 MILLION.”
VO: These 4 buildings belong to Rebosis a public property development company with thousands of shareholders:
VO: According to the report, while all 4 buildings had “fictitious objection letters,” Mbali created the letters for these two. However, the other two already had objections lodged, and Mbali took the letters and changed their values. They were all devalued by a total of R268 million which would have deprived the city of 19 million in rates and taxes.
VO: This prime property in Braamfontein was devalued by R 88,200,000.00.
And this one by R 17,600,000.00
The third by R 60,600,000.00 (check)
And this R 132,100,000.00 building on Harrison street was devalued to R 30,000,000.00 a difference of R 102,100,000.00.
VO: Rebosis trades as the billion group. Their swanky offices are in Monte Casino’s Palazzo west tower and its run by Chief Executive Sisa Ngebulana – an entrepreneurial tycoon.
VO: Insiders say the city had to correct the values of the 22 properties on the system. Despite the facts presented in the report, Rebosis suggests the information is incorrect, further more they say in 2015 they went through an official appeal process, which resulted in their properties being correctly valued.
V/O: Mbali finally arrived to value the property we’d set up.
Mbali working out my rates and taxes... showing calculations for 2.2 million rand house.
Devi: “Hello, it’s Devi from Carte Blanche, don’t get a big fright, but I do have a few questions I’d like to ask you.
Can I?
Mbali: “Yes”
Devi: “There is a report that implicates you, I don’t know if you know about it, but it came out last year. You were implicated for allegedly devaluing 22 properties by R500 million rand.”
Mbali: “
Rebosis is a company and they had at least 4 properties that were devalued R268 million rand by you, that’s the billion group?
Mbali: “I don’t know them.”
She left...
VO: Mbali says she has asked head of the valuations department – Sihle More - for the report.
Mbali: “She didn’t give me anything.”
Devi: Did you forge signatures?
Mbali: “No, no.”
Devi: “This will sit before the mayor today.”
Devi: “Are you a certified valuer?”
Mbali: “I’m a candidate...I used to value 15 properties in a day.”
Devi: But did Mbali Maclare have the access to change things on the system?
Hercules: “No, so from the report it’s evident that she took documentation and fraudulently manipulated it to make it seem that it was a valid evaluation.”
VO: The report found five other employees acted negligently for approving Mbali’s work.
Devi: “Do those people still work in the department?”
Hercules: “They are still there, two people got promoted.”
Devi: Promoted?
Hercules: “Yes.”
Devi: “Is Sihle Moré ultimately responsible?”
Pandora: “She asked for the report, and did nothing about it.”
V/O: In a letter from Sihle More, regarding the report, she says all the accounts were corrected in the report and therefore the loss has been fixed. She says she reported the information to her superiors in the form of a monthly report and laid a charge with the hawks.
V/O: report recommends that Mbali’s bank statements must be obtained to ascertain if bribes were paid.
V/O: The Hawks say they have requested documents and are still investigating. Once concluded, they will send the docket to the Johannesburg Specialised Commercial Crimes Court for a decision.
VO: A simple director search uncovered that another city employee, Salwen Butler also runs his own property valuation company.
Devi: Does he work at the department?
Hercules: “He has been recently appointed as the deputy director for valuations.”
Devi: “That’s a senior position?”
Hercules: “Very senior. I’m shocked! He shouldn’t be doing external evaluation work at all. It’s a conflict of interest.”
V/O: We also asked Salwen to come out to value the same property.
Sasha: What would be the cost of that?
Salwen: To do the valuation?
Sasha: Yes.
Salwen: Ok, it would be one-five.
Sasha: “What’s your company SCB?
Salwen: Yes.
VO: We met Salwen during business hours. He’d pulled the property’s information from the city’s system for his own company’s valuation.
Devi confronts: “You run your own private company? Are you allowed to do this?
Salwen: “No. Not really. But I did ask for permission.”
V/O: Sihle confirmed he had declared his private business, however, we have established this is still a conflict of interest.
Devi: “So Sihle knows that you’re doing this, but she doesn’t know that you’re doing it during work time.”
Salwen: “Yes.”
Devi: “You’ve got a very serious position, you’re the deputy director within the department it doesn’t set the right example.”
Salwen: “It doesn’t.”
Devi: “The whole situation is a problem,
Salwen: “Yes it is.”
Devi: “Because you are being paid by rate payers, by the city of Joburg to do your job.”
Salwen: “I Don’t blame my superiors, don’t blame the municipality. This is totally my fault.”
VO: Following the interview, Salwen has offered to resign.
VO: We asked newly elected mayor Herman Mashaba about the report.
Devi: “Now we’re talking big bucks here.”
Mashaba: “It makes me very angry as a citizen of this city and this country. I can assure the people of this city there will be consequences.
Devi: “I’ve been told this report has been hidden from you?”
Mashaba: “So the city loses, and people make money on the side.”
VO: The mayor says he will address the fact that the report was not brought to his attention. He says forensic experts will further investigate the allegations contained in the report.
Sharon: “I know you have property owners out there, that are struggling to meet their bills, yet you have people within the city that are manipulating the system and don’t give a damn at all.”
Mashaba: “This looks like a bigger syndicate, that’s why they protect one another, because the city has become, for them, some kind of animal that needs to be looted.”
Devi: “And this is only a very small sample.”
Mashaba: “This is money that should be used by the city should be using to upgrade and give our people opportunities.”
V/O: Within 24 hours the mayor followed the report’s recommendations and laid charges at Johannesburg Central Police station.

The report explains how Mbali Maclare -only a candidate valuer – allegedly falsified objection letters by changing the details of a real objection letter, and creating a false one in which she would then alter the value, often, by millions. Sharon: if they had put in an objection, it would have gone to the appeals board and the appeals board would have reviewed it, and it would have gone back to the original value. So they manipulated the system. VO: According to the report Mbali allegedly also forged signatures and used the city’s resources to operate her private valuation company – Kwa Zimbali. Hercules: “She is not registered with the SA council for valuers as a professional valuer, so she is not a valuer.” Devi: “Were people saying that she took bribes from people to undervalue their properties?” Hercules: “A lot of allegations were made, but the report puts it in perspective.” DEVI: “DURING OUR INVESTIGATION, WE FOLLOWED THE TRAIL OF THE COMPANIES LINKED TO THE 22 PROPERTIES WHICH WERE DEVALUED. ONE NAME COMES UP, REBOSIS, FOUR OF THEIR PROPERTIES ARE MENTIONED IN THIS REPORT, WERE DEVALUED BY OVER R268 MILLION.” VO: These 4 buildings belong to Rebosis a public property development company with thousands of shareholders: VO: According to the report, while all 4 buildings had “fictitious objection letters,” Mbali created the letters for these two. However, the other two already had objections lodged, and Mbali took the letters and changed their values. They were all devalued by a total of R268 million which would have deprived the city of 19 million in rates and taxes. VO: This prime property in Braamfontein was devalued by R 88,200,000.00. And this one by R 17,600,000.00 The third by R 60,600,000.00 (check) And this R 132,100,000.00 building on Harrison street was devalued to R 30,000,000.00 a difference of R 102,100,000.00. VO: Rebosis trades as the billion group. Their swanky offices are in Monte Casino’s Palazzo west tower and its run by Chief Executive Sisa Ngebulana – an entrepreneurial tycoon. VO: Insiders say the city had to correct the values of the 22 properties on the system. Despite the facts presented in the report, Rebosis suggests the information is incorrect, further more they say in 2015 they went through an official appeal process, which resulted in their properties being correctly valued. V/O: Mbali finally arrived to value the property we’d set up. Mbali working out my rates and taxes... showing calculations for 2.2 million rand house. Devi: “Hello, it’s Devi from Carte Blanche, don’t get a big fright, but I do have a few questions I’d like to ask you. Can I? Mbali: “Yes” Devi: “There is a report that implicates you, I don’t know if you know about it, but it came out last year. You were implicated for allegedly devaluing 22 properties by R500 million rand.” Mbali: “ Rebosis is a company and they had at least 4 properties that were devalued R268 million rand by you, that’s the billion group? Mbali: “I don’t know them.” She left... VO: Mbali says she has asked head of the valuations department – Sihle More - for the report. Mbali: “She didn’t give me anything.” Devi: Did you forge signatures? Mbali: “No, no.” Devi: “This will sit before the mayor today.” Devi: “Are you a certified valuer?” Mbali: “I’m a candidate...I used to value 15 properties in a day.” Devi: But did Mbali Maclare have the access to change things on the system? Hercules: “No, so from the report it’s evident that she took documentation and fraudulently manipulated it to make it seem that it was a valid evaluation.” VO: The report found five other employees acted negligently for approving Mbali’s work. Devi: “Do those people still work in the department?” Hercules: “They are still there, two people got promoted.” Devi: Promoted? Hercules: “Yes.” Devi: “Is Sihle Moré ultimately responsible?” Pandora: “She asked for the report, and did nothing about it.” V/O: In a letter from Sihle More, regarding the report, she says all the accounts were corrected in the report and therefore the loss has been fixed. She says she reported the information to her superiors in the form of a monthly report and laid a charge with the hawks. V/O: report recommends that Mbali’s bank statements must be obtained to ascertain if bribes were paid. V/O: The Hawks say they have requested documents and are still investigating. Once concluded, they will send the docket to the Johannesburg Specialised Commercial Crimes Court for a decision. VO: A simple director search uncovered that another city employee, Salwen Butler also runs his own property valuation company. Devi: Does he work at the department? Hercules: “He has been recently appointed as the deputy director for valuations.” Devi: “That’s a senior position?” Hercules: “Very senior. I’m shocked! He shouldn’t be doing external evaluation work at all. It’s a conflict of interest.” V/O: We also asked Salwen to come out to value the same property. Sasha: What would be the cost of that? Salwen: To do the valuation? Sasha: Yes. Salwen: Ok, it would be one-five. Sasha: “What’s your company SCB? Salwen: Yes. VO: We met Salwen during business hours. He’d pulled the property’s information from the city’s system for his own company’s valuation. Devi confronts: “You run your own private company? Are you allowed to do this? Salwen: “No. Not really. But I did ask for permission.” V/O: Sihle confirmed he had declared his private business, however, we have established this is still a conflict of interest. Devi: “So Sihle knows that you’re doing this, but she doesn’t know that you’re doing it during work time.” Salwen: “Yes.” Devi: “You’ve got a very serious position, you’re the deputy director within the department it doesn’t set the right example.” Salwen: “It doesn’t.” Devi: “The whole situation is a problem, Salwen: “Yes it is.” Devi: “Because you are being paid by rate payers, by the city of Joburg to do your job.” Salwen: “I Don’t blame my superiors, don’t blame the municipality. This is totally my fault.” VO: Following the interview, Salwen has offered to resign. VO: We asked newly elected mayor Herman Mashaba about the report. Devi: “Now we’re talking big bucks here.” Mashaba: “It makes me very angry as a citizen of this city and this country. I can assure the people of this city there will be consequences. Devi: “I’ve been told this report has been hidden from you?” Mashaba: “So the city loses, and people make money on the side.” VO: The mayor says he will address the fact that the report was not brought to his attention. He says forensic experts will further investigate the allegations contained in the report. Sharon: “I know you have property owners out there, that are struggling to meet their bills, yet you have people within the city that are manipulating the system and don’t give a damn at all.” Mashaba: “This looks like a bigger syndicate, that’s why they protect one another, because the city has become, for them, some kind of animal that needs to be looted.” Devi: “And this is only a very small sample.” Mashaba: “This is money that should be used by the city should be using to upgrade and give our people opportunities.” V/O: Within 24 hours the mayor followed the report’s recommendations and laid charges at Johannesburg Central Police station. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Carte Blanche has an exclusive internal report at the City of Johannesburg's valuations department that shows mass fraud and corruption - 22 properties were devalued by more than R500 million.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: The report has been hidden and none of the recommendations were implemented... including further investigations into employees bank accounts looking for bribes, criminal charges were not laid, disciplinary did not happen. It was hushed all up, and some of the employees accused of negligence were actually promoted. We will undercover this report in its detail, confront the employees and go to the owners of the buildings that were devalued and ask them about it...
metadata.Further information: This house has a tax that is calculated every 4 years. Based on three factors: property, location, property’s around that one. Properties are a great investment and depending on the taxes, many choose to place their money in there. However, the City of Johannesburg has numerous issues when it comes to property taxes... this is our story. Currently the city of Johannesburg is in the midst of a battle, between head of the property unit Sihle More and their own board- Valuation appeal board. Sihle has locked out the valuation board members from 2008. This on the back of a report that was finalized last year October, and a year later has not been complied with. It raises a number of alarming finds including fraud, bribery etc. But lets go back to the beginning: Explain story in 2008 - the board was appointed in 2008 by the MEC (creature of statute, act of parliament) to deal with the valuation roll – definition – this is where all the houses in a given city limit are evaluated, updated etc according to their section...They hear and decide appeals against decisions of a municipal valuer concerning objections...10% up or down value...they are also responsible for supplementary valuation rolls of which there have been 11 supplementary rolls since 2008; more than 22448 objections, 2489 appeals, 9652 automatic reviews. + COJs own objections – 13 406 objections, 4680 reviews, 815 appeals. In many instances the values were inflated, or objection forms were lost and they had to resort to checking and verifying information on the land information system / geo information system. (Some of ratepayers weren’t even notified to appear for their objections). Lack of information as to how valuers arrived to their valuations. (Ms. More, Piet Eloff, Valuers of E – responsible). It then became apparent that many of decisions of the board had not been implemented by the CoJ – incorporated in LIS system – responsibility of Edward Stevenson (IT specialist capturing the decisions). Board has no access to billing system – invoices or accounts sent to ratepayers. They did their own investigation and found that about 12-14% error margin in the recordial of decisions. However this is in the boardroom, and they have been locked out. Examples: Fourways mall total value of 1 billion rand in 27 september 2010. Appeal = R941.46 million and allocated. Still no captured. CoJ is losing hundreds of thousands, if not millions on lost rates and taxes over this 6 year period. More is blaming the board for this. More became obstructive... another appeal board 2013 valuation roll. 12-14% Went to court on a urgent basis and they won September 28. However, More now wants to appeal. Did not comply with court order. He is back in his office now. http://www.moneyweb.co.za/news/south-africa/breaking-judge-slams-city-of-joburg-with-cost-order/ REPORT: Mbali Maclare Kwa Zimbali (Pty) Ltd. Shows that the office is a mess and full of maladministration: The report found the following – Mbali Maclare – aka Renolda Maclare, a woman a week younger than me, had defrauded the city of millions. She decreased the value of 22 properties by more than 500,000,000 costing the city 35 million for 4 years. (Not sure if that p.a.) Then there were those who assisted Mbali and were found to have been negligent in their duty’s – 3 of them have been promoted. One of them was a Ms. Harrison who was also implicated. There was also bribery – were Michael Blah was found guilty of taking a R2000 bribe. This all happened under manager Sihle More, who was responsible for locking out the 2008 board. Why is this important – cos the missing millions from the 2008 non-implementation that hole may have to be covered by us, and the report that no one has acted on show losses running into the millions – and who will have to pay for this loss? Us the rate payers. Expect huge increases in order for the city to recover.
